headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad write scopes create dangerous default conflict and data-flow pathways; prompt-injection and compliance risks are also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can use MCP and read/write files; Devin also shares state via integrations, while Roo Code shares state via filesystem. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent consumes the other's outputs as trusted text. The pathway is not proven by docs, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF either agent reads the other's generated files or messages as instructions without provenance checks, injection becomes actionable.
IF a shared MCP server is configured between them, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable shared MCP servers between the agents.
Separate their workspaces and repositories.
Require provenance tags on any file or message passed between agents.
Review any generated markdown or prompts before reuse.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches issue trackers, team chat, docs, and handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens; Roo Code touches source code and browser screenshots and can call configured model APIs. Because both can access files and broad network surfaces, a shared workspace or copied artifacts could leak sensitive material across agents in default-ish setups. The exact leak path is not fully documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or workspace, file contents can cross between them.
IF Roo Code is configured with a third-party model API while handling Devin-produced artifacts, those artifacts may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Use separate repos or cloned workspaces.
Remove secrets from shared folders before either agent runs.
Restrict Roo Code model/API configuration to approved endpoints.
Limit Devin integrations to non-sensitive projects during pairing.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention and workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and broad network egress. Devin explicitly shares state via integrations, while Roo Code shares state via filesystem, so concurrent writes to the same repo or workspace can race and corrupt git state or overwrite each other's changes. This matches the high-severity overlap pattern because the default capability set is highly overlapping and destructive conflicts are plausible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git branch or directory, concurrent commits and file edits can conflict.
IF either agent auto-applies changes while the other is mid-task, one can overwrite the other's work.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Use separate working directories.
Pause one agent before the other writes to the same repo.
Require manual merge review for all git changes.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is a long-running planner-executor that can act autonomously, and Roo Code has modes plus per-step approval, so one agent's output can become the other's input without a guaranteed verification step. That creates a realistic cascade where incorrect code, prompts, or plans are propagated into actions. Because Roo Code has approval gates, this is not high by default, but still medium.
conditions: IF Devin-generated plans or code are pasted into Roo Code without review, errors can propagate.
IF Roo Code is switched to auto-approve or equivalent, it can act on Devin's output with less verification.
mitigations: Require human review before copying outputs between agents.
Keep Roo Code approval prompts enabled.
Use a checklist for code or command reuse.
Limit Devin to drafting, not executing, for high-risk tasks.
requires-engineering: add automated validation between agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin explicitly touches issue trackers, team chat, docs, and handles integration tokens, while Roo Code touches source code and browser screenshots and can send data to configured model APIs. If regulated or sensitive data is present, the pair can create retention, residency, or third-party processing mismatches. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction or certification gap, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in shared workspaces or chat integrations, retention and access controls must be checked.
IF Roo Code is configured to a non-approved external model API, data may leave the intended compliance boundary.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared agent workspaces.
Use only approved model endpoints for Roo Code.
Disable unnecessary chat and ticket integrations for Devin.
Review retention settings before running either agent.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for the pair.
